posts.name: keitterman
posts.cooked:
In the next edition of your card game, can you guys print a 3QR code, (sometimes called a 3D bar code) on every card?

This would be really slick, because with a small amount of space on the card’s face, you could facilitate a smart-phone style app that could be used to keep track of everything happening in the game so things don’t fall through the cracks.

Recently I picked up the Vengeance expansion and go together with my regular people to enjoy it, and although we were excited about the heroes, no one wanted to take on the villain encounter because the general consensus was: more cards in the game, more stuff gets forgotten (or even if not, the game is just elongated.) No one was thrilled to add four more villains, their cards, and the process of going through their turns.

The game is a lot of fun though.

Since we’re all software developers and designers, we had a quick conversation about how one could overcome such a challenge, and a QR code on each card would be it.

With QR codes, we could setup something like:

 

Specify hero players and turn order

Specify villain

Specify environment.

 

For each turn (villain/all heroes/environment)

Start phase:

                Show all of the math that has happened: dmg out, buffs, etc

                Have players resolve decision points (ties for most HP, selecting an ongoing to destroy, drawing a card, etc)

Main phase:

                Villian/Environment: draw and resolve a card

                Heroes: progress through the turn (draw/play/power or draw/draw)

End Phase:

               Basically a repeat of start phase, but for end-phase effects

 

Anyway, it wouldn’t take much to write a simple app to do this, and the QR codes would allow the smart-device to quickly know what is going on.  Obviously the concern is “wouldn’t it be just as easy to make an all-digital Sentinels of the Multiverse?”, but with this system, you still get the ambiance of playing a card game with friends,  and making sure everything happens true-to-form with the rules and nothing is missed (also, it wouldn’t take two hours to finish a game)

posts.cooked:
Where would you find room on the cards?

Because you can't be suggesting a QR code instead of text, surely?

It's a cool idea, but i see a bunch of people sitting around the table fiddling with their phones, getting lazy because the app will track everything, and then forgetting to scan something, which they will then fail to pick up because they aren't checking every turn.

And personally I think you need to be able to follow everything manually (so to speak) in order to understand how things work. So the app tells you you're doing 4 damage to yourself as Absolute Zero and 6 damage to another target, why those numbers? Oh no, Wraith's Razor Ordnance is only doing 4 damage now instead of 5? What happened?

posts.name: keitterman
posts.cooked:
Those are very valid points. When we were discussing it, the idea was that you wuold only have one centeral user of the smart device, passing it around for people to do their turns.

Absolutely do not replace the text, you'd have to be able to play the game without using the smart devices, it would just be an additional feature of the game. Following the game and knowing what is going on is vital to enjoying it, the app would not just "do" everything, it would have to produce a log the states why it did them, where the bonus' came from, etc. It's all the stuff you would have to explain as you were playing it, just written down, and more importantly, accurate.

Because there aren't any random factors (besides the cards being shuffled), a computer could pretty easily track the amount of cards in your hand, and such.

As for where to print them, they wouldn't have to be incedibly large, but if no space could be found on the face of the card, there's always the back (I hope no one thinks that people would start being able to read QR codes themselves)

I dunno, seemed pretty simple, but i can see your points

Just to clearify, the game would still exist exactly as it does today, but Greater Than Games adding QR codes to all of their cards allows people to develop smart-device applications that are aware of the cards that are played. That's pretty much it.

Then if you guys wanted to develop an assistant app to manage a game for people, you could, but also the open-source communities and individual groups of enthusists can write their own code that utilizes this feature to do tons of cool stuff, the one I outlined was a game manager.

 

In the gaming areana, people write mods to extend a game, make thigns easier, or whatever they like. In the card-game arena mods are pretty much periphrial hardware, like dice contains, custom tables, etc. Adding a QR code lets people write actual digital mods to the game.

 

I dunno, just a suggestion. There's a lot of card-games out there, but IMO Sentinels is the type of game that engages people. I think this could add on to that engagement as technology moves forward.

posts.cooked:
I'm with Silverleaf on this one.  QR codes have lots of really useful applications, but I don't see how injecting a middleman into the process of playing the game would really help.  We already have HP tracker apps and the Sidekick; aren't they enough?

Now, this sort of thing CAN work.  There's an app for Arkham Horror that has all of the text of all of the in-town and Other World location decks and will track them, which can save a huge amount of time spent shuffling or uselessly discarding until you get the correct card.  But for a game like Sentinels, that sort of phone interactivity isn't really needed.  (And that app doesn't use QR codes or anything, it just has a database of card text.)

posts.cooked:
Silverleaf:

I'm genuinely curious, what's the advantage?

It's just to keep track over everything on the table so you don't miss anything.

We're pretty casual players, so it's kind of a bummer when we realize we haven't been doing X dmg from some minion because we forgot after reading it or something.

Really we didn't even consider anything like this until everyone was reading over the setup for Vengence, and everyone went "well… I don't really wana keep track of 11 decks with all their cards out, lets just play vs a single boss"

 

The idea was basically just a helper app, keeps everythign straight for you. But if you don't have something as simple as scanning a QR code, then you would have to have an interface where you tell it which card was played… which would just be a solid "no, never, ever"

The game is fun because it's a card game, I dunno how fun it would be as a purely digital game, so the idea isn't to turn it in to that; it's just to leverage a smart-devices to make sure you keep track of everything.

 

I do want to say I'm a pretty big fan of SofM, you guys have done a great job. It's hard to find a game to play (board or card) that has a level of sophistication that is engaging, but not so much so that no one wants to learn how to do it.

posts.name: jagarciao
posts.cooked:
I can see the value of this to some degree... it could work with something like the Sentinels Sidekick App but instead of typing in what card you got you could just scan it when it comes into play and it automatically populates it... but that doesn't quite save you that much time.
However, if you are trying to use it to actually update the game state as the actions occur it would still be diddly and require a lot of follow up since a lot of cards have multiple actions that you may or may not do, so you would have to scan the card then take some onscreen action to identify the actions you are taking. You would also need a way to identify targets, so you might need to scan a card, then perform an onscreen action and then scan the target card. So it starts to get almost as fiddlyness as the game itself. 
 
I think such a system could work on a game if it was integrated from the start. Retrofitting an existing game into it might be more work than it is worth.

posts.name: grysqrl
posts.cooked:
I don't have a smartphone or tablet or anything like that, so I haven't really gotten to play with Sidekick. How much of this does Sidekick already take care of?

I suspect QR codes wouldn't be enough to capture the game state. Things like Galvanize, Counterpoint Bulwark, and Predator's Eye give benefits not by their presence, but by their use. Just saying "this card is on the table" wouldn't be enough to determine the state of things without one or several more scans each time they are used. This seems like it would interrupt the flow of the game, but maybe that's just me.

I also feel like QR codes would ruin the appearance of the cards. This game is really good at creating an immersive experience and putting a barcode on everything would detract from it.

I could see this as potentially a useful teaching tool (another way to visualize all of the extant effects and where they come from), but I wouldn't want it to be a permanent part of the game.
